title: Act I, Scene VII

teacherSummary.text: Alone during the feast, Macbeth weighs the murder ('If it were done when 'tis done'): Duncan is his kinsman, king and guest and a virtuous ruler, and 'bloody instructions' return to plague the inventor; he has only 'vaulting ambition.' He tells Lady Macbeth they will proceed no further. She attacks his manhood, says she would have dashed out her nursing baby's brains had she sworn to, and lays out the plan to drug the chamberlains and blame them. Macbeth agrees: 'False face must hide what the false heart doth know.'
